chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Fadala from Abu Waddad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if a man prays the two rak'ahs of the Witr, then turns away and attends to his need."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ حَاجَتَهُ: Attends to his need (often referring to relieving oneself)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to break the Witr prayer to attend to personal needs?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the flexibility of the Witr prayer, specifically permitting a break to attend to personal needs after the initial two rak'ahs. This ruling underscores the practical ease (rukhsah) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the obligatory nature of the prayer and the non-continuous requirement of its performance, thereby alleviating concerns about ritual purity or continuity during daily activities.
